about: Golden frames for blinx2 bench golden (blinx2 golden). D3D11 under Proton on the Linux/Proton host; RECOMP_DEBUG=d3d11_dump writes present 60*k+1 as frame_k. Frames are not bit-exact across runs (title-movie, idle-animation and timer phase vary with wall time), so a frame passes on an exact pixel hash or else on the tolerant compare below. Reference PNGs live in analysis/golden/frames/ (gitignored). Hashes are SHA-256 of width,height (LE u32) + RGB rows top-down.

compare.method: exact pixel hash, else per-channel mean abs diff and share of pixels off by more than pixel_tol in any channel; also the worst 64x64 tile's share of such pixels
compare.max_pace_diff_why: an anchored frame is found by flip count from its anchor, but some content follows wall time (the title's cloud movie). When a run's flips per wall second from the anchor to the frame differ from the reference run's (anchor ref_pace, or a reference's pace) by more than this share, a frame within its limits is still CLOSE (noted), one outside them is INCOMPLETE (pace mismatch) rather than FAIL, and one off at every reference by pace_fail_bad (default 0.5) of its pixels FAILs (wrong screen at any pace). No recorded pace, no check. The limit is a ratio but the harm is drift (span x ratio): override per frame for long spans. Paces for the existing references were read from their recording runs' [GPU] flip N T ms lines (2026-10-04)

frames.name: stage1-enemies-objectives
frames.note: Guards the cut-in's static content (text, rock, sky, cannon base) and gross absence of the gunners' cannons via the cannon base; the gunners' own rendering (skinning, textures, lighting, flashes, tracers) is UNCHECKED, because their band is exempt. MISSION OBJECTIVES cut-in: both Tom Tom cannon gunners, textured, skinned, lit, with muzzle flashes and tracers (the only place @stage1 shows enemies). Margin, two modes (the 3 s taps put the checkpoint at 1366-1370 or 1453-1457): in the late mode (5 of 7 runs) the A press at presents 1301-1305 opens the shot and this dump (present 1321) is 16-20 presents after it, ~70 before the closing press; in the early mode (133331, 133837) the shot opened one tap earlier, the press at 1304-1308 closes it and this dump is 13-17 presents into the close (the "Press the A Button" line gone), 45-53 before the checkpoint. 1321 is the only dump that shows the shot in both modes, and both pass the limits below. Chosen: tolerant limits, not an event anchor; anchoring the dump to the shot (followups 2) needs a dump trigger the toolkit dumper does not have. Reference: golden run 20261002-103526. The gunners' firing cycle is not tied to presents: across 7 normal runs (golden 101239, 103526; enemy 134453; shared 133954; integration 133331, 133837, 134609) pairs differ by up to mae 10.3, 21% pixels and 98% in a tile of the gunner band, while a run with the gunners and front cannon missing (RECOMP_D3D11_OCC=fixed RECOMP_ZPASS_FIXED=0, 102403) gives mae 12.9-15.8 and 23-27%. So mae (16) and bad (0.35) only catch a wholesale-wrong frame (the exempt band alone moves the frame-wide bad share by 0-14 pp) and the tiles outside the band do the work: normal runs reach 36.7% there against the reference (tile 320,320), the missing-gunner run 78.4% (cannon base, tile 256,384)

regions.why: gunner band: both gunners, cannon tops, muzzle flashes and the tracer rows (~235-260 px) animate out of phase with the dump: up to 98% in a tile between normal runs, 66-98% with the gunners missing, so no tile limit separates them here

frames.name: stage1-hud
frames.note: stg0101 gameplay: HUD, timer, radar and Stick; timer digits, radar sweep and idle pose vary: mae 0.3-2.1, 1.6-4.4% pixels. Tiles (both grids, overlap rule) outside the regions stay under 21.1% (timer digits; 253 samples, dumps 40-50 of 23 runs on the host, 2026-10-02); a missing timer, panel or radar gives 40-75%, a 100x30 block straddling tiles 31%. Known second state, open: 3 of 28 runs (070552, 072638 on 2 s taps; 101239 on 3 s taps), all with present 2641 on surface 0x00230000 (but 11 other runs on that surface are normal), show the scene with the camera ~2 px off, frames moving between dumps and the timer running ~2x (0'39"56 at dump 44, 0'51"56 at dump 50): mae 15-112, FAIL. Not a reference problem (the reference matches the normal state). Re-recorded 2026-10-02 after the character-shadow fix (toolkit e4a7db1) from golden run 20261002-191426, in which Stick stands; the old reference gave worst tile 77-81% in the Stick rect on post-fix runs. Stick's idle pose varies across runs (standing, sideways), and the Stick region's 90% tile limit covers it; the shadow itself is a small patch under his feet in every post-fix run, as in xemu. Whole-frame mae vs xemu stage1 f116 is set by that pose: 1.77 (191426, standing, the reference), 1.89 (191055), 2.20 (162307), 2.50 (191820, sideways); the old reference gave 1.74. Against the new reference: runs 162307, 191055, 191820, 192634, 193326 give mae <= 2.08, 1.9-3.4% pixels, worst tile 39.7-60.7% (all in the Stick rect); the second-state run 101239 still FAILs (mae 15.9, tile 87.8%)

This frame cannot see a missing Stick: with Stick hidden (RECOMP_D3D11_OCC=fixed RECOMP_ZPASS_FIXED=0, run 20261002-102403) its worst tile here is 83.7% and the rect-wide share 34.0%, against up to 83.9% and 32.9% (dump 44, 23 runs) with Stick drawn; no limit separates them, so stage1-stick is the missing-Stick check

stage1.followups: Structural, not done: (1) count tap periods in polls/presents, not wall seconds, so a busy host cannot move a press across an accept edge; (2) rebase dumps to events instead of fixed present numbers from boot, which carry the +-6 present stage-start jitter: done for runs that dump by flip (RECOMP_FB_DUMP_AT, golden.py dumpat; the `anchors` here), not yet for blinx2 bench's D3D11 runs, whose dumper writes every 60th present; (3) record a measured margin per frame (presents between the dump and the nearest input or scene edge) next to its limits; (4) an in-band presence region kind for stage1-enemies-objectives, independent of the gunners' phase (share of band pixels that are not sky/terrain colour, or band mean luminance against the reference with a wide tolerance), so the gunners themselves are checked

story.about: The front door from an empty save (RECOMP_SAVE_DIR=@run: bench-logs/<stamp>/save/): title, R0_opening skipped, team editor (AUTO SELECT), Story Mode / SAVE GAME, slot 1, 1P, NOW SAVING, then the Sweepers hub's CHALLENGE drill. A skips R0_opening at a varying time (tsedit opens at t=13-18 s), so @story-hub waits until t=24 and holds AUTO SELECT 8 s and the slot list 7 s: the 3 runs above put tsedit's A, state 0xD and the hub load within 0.2 dumps of each other (dumps 23.5-23.6, 53.9-54.0, 65.6-65.8). Reference: 20261003-005602 (team Steel Paw; AUTO SELECT picks the team at random, so no frame shows it)

frames.name: story-menu
frames.note: Story Mode / SAVE GAME, the slot list (slot 1 of 3 highlighted, before the 1P/2P choice); on screen from dump 55 to 61. The star and the character art behind the list animate steadily, and the menu opens (state 0xD) 231-255 flips before present 3481 depending on the run, so dump 58 catches them at different phases. That gives six exact repeat frames in 16 Proton runs (2026-10-03), in one ordered series: the further apart two phases are, the more they differ (up to bad 11.9%, worst tile 68% at 96,160 or 256,256). The differences are in the art (left half and top rows), and where it shows through the translucent list. Two references cover the series: menu-a (20261003-005602, opened ~237 flips before the dump) and menu-b (20261003-025414, ~255 flips, the latest seen; it FAILED against menu-a at bad 10.4%). Every run is within bad 3.6%, worst tile 36% of one of them; a wrong screen gives bad ~99.8%. A run that opens the menu much earlier or later than this range may FAIL; then check the phase, and anchor the dump to the menu event once golden supports that, rather than loosening the limits Re-recorded 2026-10-04: the vblank pacer fix moved the art's phase, and D3D11 runs now dump by flip so the slot-list anchor applies; menu-a re-recorded from D3D11 run 20261004-050144, menu-b (a pre-pacer phase) dropped.

frames.name: story-hub
frames.note: Sweepers hub, CHALLENGE drill 'Test 1 of 7 ... Press the A Button' (script done at dump ~65.8). The hub camera opens on one of several views at random, each fixed once the camera stops: hub-a the dish (reference run 20261003-005602), hub-b the staircase (20261003-005419), hub-c the drill wall (golden run 20261003-013300), hub-d crates and a platform (golden run 20261003-081844). Of 26 Proton story runs on 2026-10-03: hub-a 15, hub-b 9, hub-c 1, hub-d 1. Judged as a split frame (golden.py, 'split frames'): the CHALLENGE panel is held strictly and the 3D view behind it loosely. Overlay: the opaque white text (intro lines, 'Test 1 of 7', the logo's core) where all four views agree, 2931 px; 0 bad pixels in all 28 Proton runs with a dump, and leave-one-out (overlay from three views, the fourth checked) gives 0 bad for each view. Panel rects (logo, intro text, 'Test 1 of 7', 'Press the A Button'): against the run's own view, worst mae 0.91, bad 2.07%, tile 18.3% (staircase runs, 192,128). Background against its view: worst mae 0.65, bad 2.43%, tile 32.8% (the staircase's yellow ball moves); across views mae 32-61, bad 55-89%. The logo glow and 'Press the A Button' are translucent, so they can only be held against a known view. A background within the loose limits of a view names it, and the panel must then match that view. A panel that matches a view whose background does not, or a background within mae 16 of a view (the four are 32-61 apart), is a known view rendered wrong and FAILs; so does a flat background (luma std: views 29.7-76.3). Any other unseen view is NEWVIEW, which reports INCOMPLETE (not a pass): look at it, and if it is right record it with `golden.py reference story story-hub LABEL DIR` so its panel is held again. 2026-10-04: hub-b re-recorded (D3D11 run 20261004-050144, phase of the blinking 'Press the A Button' after the vblank pacer fix); hub-a re-recorded from a Mac Metal run (wt/vblcap runs/vM-s1; Mac runs open on that view); hub-c and hub-d are pre-pacer and are re-recorded when a run shows their view. The 'Press the A Button' blink is not locked to the hub anchor (panel tile 256,384 at 26-28% in anchored Mac runs).

story.followups: story-hub uses several references (hub-a dish, hub-b staircase, hub-c drill wall, hub-d crates) because the hub camera opens on a random view. Seeding the game's clock or RNG to fix the view was rejected for now as too invasive. The frame is a split frame: the opaque panel text is held in every view, the panel and background per known view; a new view reports NEWVIEW (INCOMPLETE) and, once looked at, is added with golden.py reference

Over 74-76 Metal story runs in runs/ (2026-10-02..09) the anchor's distance from the nearest reference's was p50 15-20, p90 29 (tsedit), 63 (slot-list), 45 (hub), max 81 / 63 / 112 leaving out the runs that took another menu path; 40 left 19 of 76 menu and 13 of 74 hub frames undumped (INCOMPLETE), 100 leaves one hub frame. The cost is disk until the prune: each flip of slack is one more dumped BMP (about 0.9 MB) per anchored frame, so a story run now writes up to ~600 flip dumps, ~0.55-0.7 GB (the first golden run gate: 495 dumps, 456 MB, pruned to 20 MB on its pass); a run that does not pass keeps them all
